program_name: Global Affairs: Geopolitics and Sustainability. Official Italian denomination in the ministerial course record (RAD): 'Affari globali: geopolitica e sostenibilita''; official English denomination: 'Global affairs: geopolitics and sustainability'. Internal University of Trento course code 0631H; CINECA/course-catalogue id 10905. Two-year second-cycle Master's degree (laurea magistrale), 120 CFU/ECTS, offered by the Department of Sociology and Social Research (Dipartimento di Sociologia e Ricerca Sociale, DSRS). It is formally a MODIFICATION of the previous Master's degree 'Studi globali e locali' / 'Global and Local Studies' (GLOCAL, ministerial id 1397284) and has replaced it from academic year 2025/2026; departmental abbreviation 'GLOBAL'. Approved by the teaching structure on 06/11/2024 and by the Academic Senate / Board of Governors on 26/02/2025.
teaching_language: CATEGORY (3) - MIXED 'English and Italian'. This is NOT a fully English-taught programme and it is NOT an English percorso inside an Italian degree: it is a single, genuinely bilingual curriculum. Evidence, in decreasing order of authority: (1) The ministerial course record (RAD, 'Regolamento didattico di ateneo' extract published by UniTrento) states verbatim 'Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: italiano, inglese' and, in the description of the learning outcomes, 'La laurea magistrale offre corsi obbligatori sia in italiano che in lingua inglese che, attraverso una didattica partecipativa, consentono alle/agli studenti di esercitare le loro capacita' di espressione scritta e verbale in piu' lingue' ('the master's degree offers compulsory courses both in Italian and in English which, through participatory teaching, allow students to practise their written and verbal expression skills in several languages'). (2) The official programme page corsi.unitn.it shows in its 'IN SHORT' box 'LANGUAGE: English Italian' and, under 'How you'll learn', 'Courses in Italian and English with a strong intercultural focus'; the learning outcomes include 'communicate effectively in multicultural environments, in Italian and English'. (3) For non-European applicants the programme is admitted ONLY through the 'Bando unico di Ateneo per l'ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale IN LINGUA ITALIANA' (single University call for admission to master's degrees TAUGHT IN ITALIAN) - i.e. UniTrento itself administratively classifies it as an Italian-language master's degree - and Italian at CEFR B2 is a hard admission requirement there. (4) Italian B2 is also required on the free-access (European) route for every applicant without Italian citizenship. PRACTICAL LANGUAGE MAP (from the official Department of Sociology and Social Research student handbook 'GUIDA STUDENTI A.A. 2026-2027', which prints the study plan with each course's official title): YEAR 1 - all six compulsory taught courses carry English titles and are delivered in English: Global history: the post-1989 world order (136110, 6 CFU, J. Monnet Chair-COTPA), Global cultures (136111, 6), International political economy (135765, 6), Geopolitics in a global word [sic] (136112, 6), Qualitative research methods (135767, 9), Quantitative research methods (135768, 9); plus 3 CFU of compulsory language skills taken as 'Seminar: Developing academic texts and presentations' (136084, 36 hours, an ENGLISH academic-skills seminar) or as an English C1/C2 exam/certificate. YEAR 2 - the elective groups MIX English-titled and Italian-titled courses: English-titled - Global challenges to democracy (136115), Communication and politics (136114), Environmental sustainability in a globalized world (136117), Communication, Science and Technologies (135287), International sustainable development: methods and project (135947), Sociology of collective action (135298), plus two School of International Studies courses open as free-choice, The Politics of China: Past and Present (155422) and History and International relations of the middle east (155418); Italian-titled - Teoria e pratica della negoziazione nelle Istituzioni (136120), Migrazioni, confini, cittadinanza (136134), Questioni di genere: attori, processi, politiche (136116), Stati e potere globale. Territorio, Confini, Autonomie (136119), L'Africa nelle relazioni internazionali (136133), Transizione sostenibile e territorio (136121), Antropologia dei domini collettivi e dei territori di vita (136096). [uncertain] Counting the English-titled options only, a second-year study plan could arithmetically be assembled entirely in English (1 of 2 in the first elective group, 2 of 4 in the second, 2 of 6 in the third are English-titled), but this could NOT be verified course-by-course against the official syllabi, because the UniTrento/CINECA Course Catalogue - the only official source that publishes each course's 'lingua di erogazione' - is behind an AWS WAF human-verification gate. Note also that the English-language version of corsi.unitn.it TRANSLATES the Italian-taught course titles into English (for example 'Migrazioni, confini, cittadinanza' appears there as 'Migration, borders, citizenship' and 'Teoria e pratica della negoziazione nelle Istituzioni' as 'Theory and practice of negotiation in institutions'), which makes the curriculum look fully English on the English site when it is not. Two further Italian-language elements: the Department's official programme handbook ('Guida SRS') exists in Italian only, and the department's own course index links this programme's site under the Italian path corsi.unitn.it/it/global-affairs-geopolitics-and-sustainability while it links the genuinely English DSRS masters (Data Science, Sociology and Social Research) under /en/.

degree_class: LM-62 R - 'Scienze della politica' (Political sciences). The RAD states 'Classe: LM-62 R - Scienze della politica'; the Department handbook heading reads 'GLOBAL - CORSO DI LAUREA MAGISTRALE IN GLOBAL AFFAIRS: GEOPOLITICS AND SUSTAINABILITY - CLASSE LM-62 SCIENZE DELLA POLITICA'; the University's admission-requirements table for Italian-taught master's degrees lists the course under 'Classe: LM62R'. The trailing 'R' marks the class as re-designed under Ministerial Decree 1649/2023 (the 'riprogettazione' of the degree classes), not a different class. This matches the degree_class_hint 'LM62'.
admission_type: TWO DIFFERENT ROUTES, depending on the applicant's category (check at www.unitn.it/en/check-your-category). (A) EUROPEANS AND EQUIVALENTS (EU/EEA citizens, Italian citizens, and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy): OPEN / FREE ACCESS ('accesso libero', 'The programme is free access to European citizens and equivalents'; the handbook adds 'Il corso e' ad accesso libero per gli studenti con cittadinanza europea e per gli studenti con cittadinanza extraeuropea residenti in Italia'). There is no numero programmato, no ranking and no entrance test on this route: admission is a verification of the curricular and language requirements, plus - only if the bachelor's final grade is below 90/110 - a selection interview with the President of the programme. (B) NON-EUROPEANS RESIDING OUTSIDE ITALY: RESTRICTED ACCESS with a reserved quota of 4 places, awarded through a competitive public selection under the university-wide call 'Bando unico di Ateneo per l'ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale in lingua italiana', academic year 2026/2027 (Rectoral Decree 1419/2025 of 16 December 2025, Annex 1). That selection is a dossier evaluation scored out of 100 by a commission appointed by Rectoral Decree, with a possible online interview; eligibility threshold 50/100; one ranking per programme; ties broken in favour of the younger candidate; unassigned non-European places are released to 'Europeans and equivalents' within the limits of the table. Applicants may apply to a maximum of 2 programmes in the same application. NO TOLC, NO SAT, NO GRE/GMAT and no written entrance examination on either route.
application_deadline_eu: Academic year 2026/2027 (Europeans and equivalents, free-access route): admission application ('Richiesta di ammissione') open FROM 17 APRIL 2026 TO 11 DECEMBER 2026, submitted at https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/en/Web/GoHome/ammissione/RVRCALMSoc26 . It must be submitted by ALL applicants, including students already enrolled in a UniTrento programme and including those who already meet every requirement; it may be submitted before graduating or before all requirements are met, and the outcome is communicated by e-mail. ENROLMENT (immatricolazione) deadline for a.y. 2026/2027: 21 DECEMBER 2026. After receiving the matriculation number the student must complete the 'yearly enrolment' within 7 days. Missing curricular credits may be made up through 'Single courses for master's degrees' with the exams passed by the enrolment deadline; a missing English B2 may be made up at the University Language Centre (CLA) - the 2026 CLA English test sessions for master's admission are: session 1 registration 27 March-20 April, written 27 April, oral 8 May; session 2 registration 20 April-15 May, written 25 May, oral 5 June; session 3 registration 15 May-25 June, written 6 July, oral 17 July; session 4 registration 25 June-21 August, written 2 September, oral 11 September; session 5 registration 21 August-2 October, written 12 October, oral 23 October; session 6 registration 2 October-13 November, written 23 November, oral 4 December (written part in person at the CLA in Trento, speaking part online).
application_deadline_non_eu: Academic year 2026/2027 (non-Europeans residing outside Italy, 4 reserved places): a single window closing at 12:00 noon Italian time (GMT+1) on 4 MARCH 2026, through the online application 'Accesso ai corsi di laurea magistrale per cittadini e cittadine di paesi non appartenenti all'Unione Europea e non residenti in Italia per l'a.a. 2026/2027' at https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/it/Web/Home/ammissione (the English page links https://webapps.unitn.it/Apply/it/MyUnitn/Home/133084/ammissione/contingLM26). The account must be created first - recommended at least three working days before the deadline. Non-refundable application fee EUR 30.00, payable by the deadline; unpaid applications are excluded and not evaluated. Applicants still to graduate are admitted provided the bachelor's degree is obtained BY 30 JUNE 2026. Ranking published by 24 APRIL 2026 on the 'Ammissione ad un corso in lingua italiana' page. Admitted candidates pay a non-refundable place-confirmation fee of EUR 100.00 by the date stated in the ranking (failure to confirm = forfeiture; vacated places pass to the next eligible candidate). Confirmed candidates must then complete Universitaly pre-enrolment at the competent Italian diplomatic representation within the dates set by the annual ministerial circular (published around March) - pre-enrolment is compulsory in order to obtain the study visa. FINAL DEADLINE FOR ARRIVAL AT THE UNIVERSITY OF TRENTO: 30 SEPTEMBER 2026, on pain of forfeiture of admission, with no extension granted even for reasons beyond the candidate's control. Enrolment timetables are announced after the ranking is published. Note: there is no second/later non-EU session for this programme.
entry_exam_or_test: No standardised entrance test of any kind (no TOLC, no CEnT, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT) and no written admission exam. (A) EUROPEANS AND EQUIVALENTS: admission is by requirement check only. An INTERVIEW is triggered in one case - a bachelor's final grade below 90/110: 'You must have a graduation grade of minimum 90/110, or equivalent. With a lower mark you need to pass an admission interview with the programme's president.' Student Support puts the candidate in touch with the President of the programme by e-mail. Separately, an applicant who cannot certify English B2 may sit the CLA English proficiency test for master's admission (six 2026 sessions; written in person in Trento, oral online) - a pass/fail requirement-recovery test, not a competitive exam. (B) NON-EUROPEANS: the commission scores the application dossier out of 100 using the criteria published in the annex 'Tabella requisiti di ammissione e punteggi per la valutazione'. For this programme the bands are: merit (bachelor's grade) 0-15 points, awarded only above the 80% threshold (81-87% = 5 points, 88-94% = 10 points, 95-100% = 15 points); language 0-10 extra points for English above B2 (C1 = 6 points, C2 = 10 points); 'curriculum studiorum ed altre attivita' personali' 0-20 points; relevance/assessment of the knowledge acquired in the previous degree 0-55 points. Minimum admission score 50/100, maximum 100/100. The commission requests an interview only from admissible candidates scoring at least 35 in the previous-career knowledge assessment, and the interview also assesses the candidate's English. A further remote interview may be requested whenever the submitted documents do not allow an adequate evaluation. Italian language proficiency is verified separately on a pass/fail basis (including, if needed, the CISIA Italian L2 test, for which UniTrento organises an ad hoc session on 26 March 2026) and does NOT contribute to the ranking score.
academic_requirements: PLACES: no cap for Europeans and equivalents (free access). 4 places reserved for non-Europeans residing outside Italy in a.y. 2026/2027 (out of 45 non-EU places distributed across the 13 Italian-taught master's degrees in the university-wide call). Unassigned non-EU places are made available to Europeans and equivalents within the limits of the table. QUALIFICATION: a bachelor's degree ('laurea') or university diploma from a programme of at least three years' duration, or an equivalent qualification, including one obtained abroad if recognised as suitable. An Italian bachelor's degree is directly eligible if it belongs to class L-36 (Political science and international relations), L-37 (Social sciences for cooperation, development and peace / Peace studies), L-39 (Social work) or L-40 (Sociology). CURRICULAR CREDITS FOR ALL OTHER DEGREE CLASSES (and the yardstick used to assess foreign degrees): at least 36 ECTS/CFU in at least one of the scientific-disciplinary sectors SPS/04, SPS/07, SECS-P/02, IUS/09, M-STO/04 (renamed in the 2026/27 handbook as GSPS-02/A, GSPS-05/A, ECON-02/A, GIUR-05/A, HIST-03/A) AND at least 12 ECTS/CFU in at least one of SECS-S/04, SPS/01, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, M-DEA/01, M-GGR/02 (renamed STAT-03/A, GSPS-01/A, GSPS-06/A, GSPS-08/A, GSPS-08/B, GSPS-07/A, SDEA-01/A, GEOG-01/B). Substantively these are: political science, sociology of political phenomena, economic policy, public/international law, contemporary history, plus statistics, general sociology, sociology of culture and communication, sociology of economic processes and labour, environmental and territorial sociology, political-economic geography and demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines. The RAD is explicit that 'non e' ammessa l'assegnazione di debiti formativi od obblighi formativi aggiuntivi' - no additional educational debts (OFA) may be assigned, so the curricular requirements must be complete before the personal-preparation check; UniTrento's remedy is enrolment in 'Single courses for master's degrees' with the missing exams passed before the enrolment deadline. PERSONAL PREPARATION: bachelor's final grade of at least 90/110 (or equivalent); below that, a selection interview with the President of the programme is compulsory. For the NON-EU selection the equivalent merit threshold is 80% of the maximum grade of the applicant's own grading scale, and an application below 80% is only admissible after an interview with the commission assessing the eligibility of the candidacy; in addition the previous degree must include exams in at least two of the following areas: political science, general sociology, economic policy, public-law institutions, contemporary history, political economy, history of economic thought, sociology of cultural and communicative processes, sociology of economic and labour processes, environmental and territorial sociology, sociology of political phenomena, political-economic geography, demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines. Non-EU applicants who have not yet graduated are admitted provided the degree is obtained by 30 June 2026; UniTrento may require a CIMEA Statement of Verification and/or Statement of Comparability for foreign qualifications. Non-EU transfers from another university and admission to the second year are possible only after passing this same selection and subject to available places and the programme regulations.
language_requirements: ENGLISH - ADMISSION: minimum CEFR B2, required of every applicant on both routes. On the European/free-access route it must be proven by 'a language certificate or university exam recognised by UniTrento' - specifically the international certificates listed by the Department of Sociology and Social Research in its recognised-certificates table, or a university language exam recognised by the Department. Applicants who cannot certify it may recover the requirement by passing the CLA (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) English test for master's admission; once passed, the student e-mails Student Support to proceed with enrolment. On the non-EU route English B2 is a stated linguistic requirement in the admission-requirements table and is additionally verified during the interview when one is held; levels above B2 earn bonus ranking points (C1 = 6, C2 = 10). ITALIAN - ADMISSION: a genuine and decisive requirement. corsi.unitn.it states 'If you do not have Italian citizenship, you must show proof of Italian proficiency at least at the B2 level of the CEFR'; the RAD states 'Nel caso di studente straniero, l'accesso al CdS e' subordinato al possesso dei requisiti precedenti e, inoltre: conoscenza della lingua italiana almeno a livello B2'; the Department handbook repeats it and adds that it may be demonstrated either by a certificate recognised by the Department or by a test at the CLA. For NON-EU applicants the university-wide call makes Italian B2 an absolute admission requirement ('La dimostrazione della conoscenza della lingua italiana e' uno dei requisiti di ammissione, in mancanza del quale non e' possibile essere ammessi'), provable by: (i) a CILS, CELI, PLIDA or ROMA3 certificate (CLIQ quality system) - a provisional declaration of having passed the level may be attached if the certificate has not yet been issued; (ii) the CISIA Italian L2 test with a score of at least 52/72 (120 minutes; listening, reading, language structures; 72 items) taken at any centre by 4 March 2026, or at the ad hoc UniTrento session on 26 March 2026 (registration is made inside the admission application; a stable internet connection, a PC and a camera-and-microphone mobile device are required); (iii) exemptions - a five-year or four-year Italian upper-secondary diploma obtained at Italian state or state-recognised schools abroad, one of the final secondary-school qualifications listed in Annex 2 of the ministerial circular, Argentinian secondary certificates attesting at least 5 years of Italian teaching under Law 210/1999, or a Diploma in Italian language and culture from the Universita' per Stranieri of Perugia or Siena. The Italian check is pass/fail and does not contribute to the ranking score. LANGUAGE DURING THE DEGREE: the study plan contains 3 compulsory CFU of language skills, obtained either through the 'Seminar: Developing academic texts and presentations' (course 136084, 36 hours, offered in both semesters, restricted number of places and compulsory attendance, reserved to the GLOBAL, OST and MOVASS master's students, designed to build English academic presentation, discussion, writing and comprehension skills; it may also be taken as a non-attending student with a language test if the student already has advanced skills) or through the 'Competenze linguistiche - Inglese C1' (135249) / 'C2' (135250) exam or a recognised certificate; C1/C2 additionally bring 4 extra free-choice credits. Exams in further foreign languages can earn credits within the 'Other activities' allowance, per the Department's foreign-language credit-recognition table for this programme. Previously passed language exams are recognisable for the compulsory language requirement only if passed within the last 5 years. The RAD's expected outcome is fluent written and spoken English at 'at least advanced B2'.
required_documents: [uncertain] EUROPEANS AND EQUIVALENTS: UniTrento does not publish a document checklist for the free-access admission request on the programme pages; the online admission form at webapps.unitn.it/Apply (.../ammissione/RVRCALMSoc26) collects the evidence, and in substance the applicant must document the bachelor's degree/enrolment and transcript (to prove the L-36/L-37/L-39/L-40 class or the 36+12 ECTS sectors and the 90/110 grade), an English B2 certificate or recognised university language exam, and - for anyone without Italian citizenship - evidence of Italian at B2. Foreign-qualification holders are separately handled through the University's 'Evaluation of foreign qualifications' procedure and may be asked for CIMEA Statements of Verification/Comparability. This list is inferred from the published requirements, not quoted from an official checklist, hence flagged as uncertain. NON-EUROPEANS (exhaustive, quoted from Art. 4.3 of the 2026/2027 university-wide call): (a) copy of the passport - personal-data pages only; (b) copy of the degree certificate, or a certificate of enrolment stating the expected graduation date, officially translated into English or Italian; (c) transcript of records indicating study programme, duration, grade obtained and the reference grading scale, officially translated into English or Italian; (d) certificates of any further post-graduate qualifications already held at the time of application, with programme, duration, grade and grading scale, officially translated; (e) certificates of language and/or IT skills; (f) 'curriculum vitae et studiorum' WRITTEN IN ITALIAN in the European format; (g) the Italian language certificate, or a declaration of falling within one of the exemption cases, or a declaration of intent to sit the Italian test at the University of Trento. Plus the EUR 30.00 non-refundable application fee paid by the deadline (non-payment = exclusion). Up to 2 programmes may be selected in one application, and the form also allows the applicant to ask for advice on the most suitable master's programme and to request a preliminary evaluation for admission to the second year. Later stages: EUR 100.00 place-confirmation fee, Universitaly pre-enrolment at the Italian diplomatic representation, study visa, arrival in Trento by 30 September 2026.

uncertainty_notes: 1) THE LANGUAGE DISCREPANCY FLAGGED IN THE BRIEF IS REAL AND IS RESOLVED AGAINST 'ENGLISH'. The 'English' marking comes from the University orientation portal orienta.unitn.it, whose entry for this programme states 'Durata e lingua del corso: 2 anni, in inglese'. That entry is a stale carry-over: its URL is still /cosa-scegliere/317/global-and-local-studies, and its student testimonial still refers to the predecessor degree 'Global and Local Studies' (GLOCAL), which WAS a fully English-taught LM-62. From a.y. 2025/2026 that degree was re-designed into 'Global Affairs: Geopolitics and Sustainability' and the language was changed to Italian + English. Every higher-authority source disagrees with the orienta label: the ministerial RAD ('Lingua in cui si tiene il corso: italiano, inglese'; 'La laurea magistrale offre corsi obbligatori sia in italiano che in lingua inglese'), the programme page itself ('LANGUAGE: English Italian', 'Courses in Italian and English'), and above all the university's administrative treatment of the programme - non-European applicants can only enter it through the 'Bando unico di Ateneo per l'ammissione ai corsi di laurea magistrale IN LINGUA ITALIANA'. TEACHING_LANGUAGE SHOULD THEREFORE BE RECORDED AS MIXED (English and Italian), NOT as English. 2) PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE FOR NON-ITALIAN-SPEAKING APPLICANTS - THE DECISIVE POINT: ITALIAN AT CEFR B2 IS AN ADMISSION REQUIREMENT FOR EVERY APPLICANT WITHOUT ITALIAN CITIZENSHIP, on both the free-access European route and the non-European quota route, and it must be held BEFORE enrolment (there is no post-enrolment make-up path published for Italian, unlike English which can be recovered at the CLA). For a Turkish or other non-EU applicant this means: CILS/CELI/PLIDA/ROMA3 at B2, or the CISIA Italian L2 test at 52/72 or better, in addition to English B2. This programme is therefore NOT realistically open to a candidate with no Italian, even though its English-language marketing page and the orienta portal can give that impression. 3) COURSE-LEVEL LANGUAGE SPLIT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED FROM SYLLABI. The classification of individual courses above is inferred from the official course TITLES as printed in the Department's Italian-language handbook (English titles = English delivery, Italian titles = Italian delivery), which is UniTrento's consistent practice, but the only official source publishing each course's 'lingua di erogazione' is the CINECA Course Catalogue (unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2025/10905), which is protected by an AWS WAF human-verification challenge that was not bypassed. The arithmetic claim that a second-year study plan could be assembled entirely from English-titled courses is therefore unverified; it also does not change the fact that Italian B2 is required at admission. 4) THE ENGLISH VERSION OF corsi.unitn.it TRANSLATES ITALIAN-TAUGHT COURSE TITLES INTO ENGLISH, which is the main mechanism by which this programme reads as fully English to an international applicant. Examples: 'Migrazioni, confini, cittadinanza' appears as 'Migration, borders, citizenship'; 'Questioni di genere: attori, processi, politiche' as 'Gender issues: actors, processes, policies'; 'Stati e potere globale. Territorio, Confini, Autonomie' as 'States and Global Power: Territory, Borders, Autonomy'; 'Transizione sostenibile e territorio' as 'Sustainable transition and territory'; 'Teoria e pratica della negoziazione nelle Istituzioni' as 'Theory and practice of negotiation in institutions'. 5) MINOR OFFER DISCREPANCY BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL SOURCES for the second-year electives: the corsi.unitn.it 'Overview' page (snapshot March 2026) lists 'People, Politics and the Planet' (155342) among the third elective group and does not list 'Communication, Science and Technologies' (135287) or 'L'Africa nelle relazioni internazionali' (136133), whereas the Department handbook for 2026/2027 (version dated July 2026, the more recent document) lists the latter two and not the former. Elective offers vary year to year; the handbook was preferred. 6) ACCESS AND DOCUMENTS ON THE EUROPEAN ROUTE ARE UNDER-DOCUMENTED PUBLICLY: UniTrento publishes no document checklist and no formal call for the free-access route, so required_documents for that route is an inference from the stated requirements and is flagged [uncertain]. 7) SSD CODE MIGRATION: the corsi.unitn.it admission page and the RAD still use the OLD scientific-disciplinary sector codes (SPS/04, SPS/07, SECS-P/02, IUS/09, M-STO/04 and SECS-S/04, SPS/01, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, SPS/11, M-DEA/01, M-GGR/02), while the 2026/2027 handbook uses the NEW codes (GSPS-02/A, GSPS-05/A, ECON-02/A, GIUR-05/A, HIST-03/A; STAT-03/A, GSPS-01/A, GSPS-06/A, GSPS-08/A, GSPS-08/B, GSPS-07/A, SDEA-01/A, GEOG-01/B). These are the same requirements expressed in the old and new ministerial nomenclature. 8) A LIKELY TYPO IN THE OFFICIAL CALL: Art. 7.4 sets the second-year fee exemption on credits acquired 'entro la scadenza del 10 agosto 2026' although it describes the end of the FIRST year of a course starting in 2026/2027 - the intended date is almost certainly 10 August 2027. The credit thresholds themselves (36 / 24-35 / 18-23 / <18 CFU) are quoted as printed. Similarly the annex is titled 'Allegato 1 - Tabella requisiti' inside a file named 'Allegato2_Tabella1_26_27.pdf'; both refer to the same document, the requirements/scoring table of Rectoral Decree 1419/2025. 9) SOURCE ACCESS METHOD: corsi.unitn.it, www.unitn.it and unitn.coursecatalogue.cineca.it are all behind an AWS WAF and returned HTTP 405 (or a human-verification page in a real browser) to every direct request. All content from those hosts was read through Internet Archive raw ('id_') snapshots, which return the original bytes - snapshot dates: programme home 11 March 2026, overview 11 March 2026, admission page (English) 15 April 2026, admission page (Italian) 12 April 2026, language proficiency 15 April 2026, lessons/syllabus 10 April 2026, contacts 8 December 2025, 'Admission to courses taught in Italian' 12 April 2026; the two call annexes and the RAD were downloaded as genuine PDFs (Annex 1 verified by MD5 against an independently retrieved copy) and text-extracted in full. Two UniTrento properties were reachable live and were used as independent, same-day (31 August 2026) confirmation: www.sociologia.unitn.it (the 2026/2027 handbook PDF, 2.16 MB, 144 pages) and orienta.unitn.it. Because the corsi.unitn.it snapshots date from spring 2026, applicants should re-check the live pages before applying; the 17 April - 11 December 2026 European window in particular was still open at the time of research. 10) NOT VERIFIED / OUT OF SCOPE: exact EU/equivalent (ISEE-banded) tuition amounts were not retrieved, since the relevant www.unitn.it fee pages were neither directly reachable nor archived - only the official page URLs and the non-EU amounts stated verbatim in the call are reported. The programme is also listed among those eligible for the university's 'Talete' Honours Programme and offers the ESST international excellence track and internship/study-abroad options, but those are post-enrolment opportunities with separate calls and are not part of the admission requirements.
